title: The Fortress of Terror
text: “Fatheeeeeeeer, my Faaaaatheeeeer!”
I blasted forward in Drive Mode, racing straight for the fortress on the border. But by the time I arrived, there was no sign of anyone resembling Father.
“W-what is that!?”
“A monster!?”

I could see soldiers at the fortress pointing at me, but that was none of my concern. Perhaps we’d missed each other, and Father was taking some detour along the way… or perhaps he was even now being tortured within this very fortress. If that were the case, blasting the place to smithereens with magic might catch him in the crossfire too. So I made a sharp, skillful drift—kiki-screech!—changed course, and retreated far enough that the soldiers could no longer spot me. Then I switched to cloaking mode to investigate the inside of the fortress properly.
“What the heck was that weird human-tank thing kicking up all that dust earlier?”
“No idea… have you ever seen a monster like that?”
“Maybe something they cooked up in a research lab?”

The soldiers inside the fortress were gathered together, buzzing with speculation. A strict checkpoint had been set up as well, with long lines of merchants and adventurers waiting to pass through. It seemed that Father leaving the country was an extremely inconvenient outcome for these people. Since they were still running checkpoints, I supposed that meant Father hadn’t been captured yet—but just in case, I ought to search the fortress thoroughly. Using phasing to pass through walls, I combed every corner of the place.
“According to our information, the shield devil is planning to join up with the Siltvelt scum and slip out of the country. We cannot, under any circumstances, allow their leader to escape!”

There, in the fortress command room, the knight commander was bellowing at the top of his lungs. So he was here after all. Now that I thought about it, this fellow had also shown up during the loop when we went to Siltvelt. According to what I’d heard, in the very first world, he’d been the one giving orders to attack Father and the others while they were defending Lute Village.
“Search every blade of grass if you have to! Find them and blast them to pieces, demi-humans and all!”
“Yes, sir!”
His subordinates filed out of the room wearing expressions that practically screamed how many times is this now, before disappearing.
“Hmph…”

The knight commander stood there, arms crossed, looking terribly pleased with himself. As I later learned, he’d only recently been appointed to his position. Apparently the original knight commander had been dismissed amid the political upheaval that followed the queen’s disappearance and the summoning of the Heroes. Factional politics, I suppose you’d call it.
“Well then… guess I’ll head to the wine cellar.”

…Behavior remarkably similar to that armor fellow who joins up with Itsuki. Looking closer, I thought the face looked similar too. Relatives, perhaps? In any case, him being alone was extremely convenient for me. This was my first time reaching this particular branch point—though it was a continuation of the loop, it was a world that had rewound somewhat. No loop existed where Father met his end here. Still, I had unfinished business to settle, and revenge to take for that humiliating loop.
“Ugh—”

So, just as he reached out to open the door on his way to steal from the wine cellar, faster than his hand could touch it… I ran him clean through with my spear. Since he seemed about to scream just like that armor fellow had, I used Silence Spear. If they really were relatives, there was a good chance they’d scream the same way too.
Just as I’d predicted, he tried to let out a scream at the sight of the spear jutting from his own back. I sealed off the surrounding air with magic to muffle the sound as best I could, and then—
“Burst Lance X!”
Poof! I reduced him to ash in an instant.

The ashes scattered and dissolved into dust, smoke drifting through the room, but no soldiers seemed to have noticed the commotion. That settled one score from that humiliating loop! I’d already beaten him senseless once when we went to Siltvelt, but this was a perfectly good opportunity to finish the job.
“Fuhahaha, indeed. Now then… where might Father be?”

Well, judging from what this fellow had said just before I dispatched him, it seemed Father hadn’t arrived at this fortress yet. Either way, the clock was ticking. And so I decided to leave the fortress and go searching for him. I suspected Father was staying somewhere in one of the towns along the direct route between the fortress and Melromarc Castle… but searching by scent alone would cover far too wide an area. What’s more, since he was traveling by carriage, all sorts of scents would be mixed together, making it difficult to pin down. I thought it best to focus my search on the places I’d visited during the Siltvelt trip, but it seemed they’d taken a different road than the one I remembered, so I couldn’t find them. Perhaps, out of caution, they’d deliberately chosen a different route than before. With no other option, I decided to wait for Father somewhere within sight of the fortress… but night fell before he appeared.
“Father…”

I needed to remain extremely vigilant. Could I really say there was zero chance they might pass by here even if I went back now? I’d heard that some demi-humans and beastmen were nocturnal. Which meant Father might well be brought to the border under cover of night. And so, a sleepless vigil it would be.

Ah, Father… I only wished he were safe. At one point I heard a commotion stirring near the fortress, so I crept closer to investigate, and found them in an uproar over the knight commander having gone missing. Well, of course—I was the one who’d disposed of him. HAHAHA.

At least it seemed Father hadn’t been captured while I’d been out searching—that much was a relief. But the fortress folk were talking about sending messengers to search the surrounding towns. If that caused Father’s group to change their route, it would be quite a problem.

Honestly, what a troublesome bunch. Perhaps I ought to just assassinate the lot of them? Yes, that sounded about right. I’d dispose of them quietly, in secret. Just as I’d cornered Takt back on Nanatsuki Island, I would pick off any soldier foolish enough to wander around alone, one by one. And so, to pass the time through the night, I quietly went about eliminating soldiers who appeared to belong to the Three Heroes Church, one after another.
“Something’s not right here… people keep disappearing from the fortress, one after another.”
“No way, man. You’re just being paranoid. Watch, I’ll go check it out myself.”
“H-hey, wait…”
The soldier wandered casually into an empty, deserted building, so I figured I’d dispatch him the same way I had the knight commander.
“Hey. You okay in there?”

“Oh come on, quit being such a coward. Sheesh, the shield devil’s supposedly on his way here any minute, and you’re all jumpy over nothing. They say demi-humans and beastmen can sneak up without making a sound—so if anything weird happens, it’s a safe bet they’re behind it.”

Sense out their presence, he says—for all his tough talk, he clearly hadn’t noticed my presence at all. Heh… if it were Big Sister, perhaps, but the likes of you noticing my presence? A thousand years too early for that. Someone on Éclair’s level might catch on from a careless noise, perhaps.
“You don’t think the Spear Hero’s behind this, do you? Like some vengeful spirit tied to that weird thing that showed up during the day…”

“No way in hell. That dopey-looking idiot? Pull off something that impressive? I saw it myself—the way he got played by that woman the kingdom set him up with, eyes spinning in circles. Man, I could barely hold in my laughter.”
…Completely guilty. He would pay for mocking Father with his very life.
“Still… he’s a Hero who came from another world and doesn’t know anything, right? Kind of feel sorry for the guy.”
“What are you even saying? Don’t tell me you actually worship the shield devil or something?”
“Well, he’s a Hero in other countries, isn’t he? It’s just that back home we’ve got the Four Heroes Church crowd, so…”
“Don’t let them fool you. There’s no way some blockhead like that could ever save the world.”
Guilty. He, too, would atone with his life.
“Hm? What was that—”
And right there, the soldier’s voice cut off.
“H-hey. Don’t scare me like that… hey? Cut it out with the pranks! Hey!”
I decided to let this one off the hook, since he’d shown a bit of sympathy for Father. He went searching for the friend I’d already disposed of earlier, but of course, there was nothing left to find.
“C-could it be… really… u-uwaaaaaaaaaaaah!”

And with that, the soldier I’d spared let out a scream and bolted from the fortress, vanishing into the night. And so the night passed. By morning, the fortress was left with nothing but the terrified stragglers who’d spent the entire night in fear, and the moment the sun rose, they too fled the place entirely. Well, in any case, that was one less thing to worry about.
